decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit, when it lands no bash?
decisions.ruling: Yes. The plan lands TOML only, but mise bootstrap installs what it declares: two third-party Homebrew taps (stablyai/orca, saffsanity/sill), 52 package ids and macOS defaults. One review unit in wave 2 covers U1, U2 and U3; it covers edit units alone, so it runs the security half.
decisions.rejected: No review unit: the wave review alone does not run /security-review over the taps and the package ids.

decisions.decision: Can the 16 plans of the merge run in parallel?
decisions.ruling: No. The 16 plans form one linear chain through requires, because most of them edit sync-engine/repo-sync or sync-engine/setup-sync, and parallel plans conflict there. This plan requires 2026-11-04-macos-tools-extras.

decisions.decision: Six of the 52 tools have mise sections other than [bootstrap.packages]. What happens to them?
decisions.ruling: Each section moves into tools.toml as a [mise.*] table with its keys unchanged: opencode and sublime-text [mise.shell_alias]; gcloud [mise.tools.gcloud] and [mise.env]; orca and sill [mise.bootstrap.brew.taps]; vorssaint [mise.bootstrap.macos.defaults."com.vorssaint.utils"]. Each tool still ships no file other than tools.toml.
decisions.rejected: Drop the extra sections; this loses live behavior (aliases, env, taps, the vorssaint defaults).

decisions.decision: Do the comments of the old mise fragments stay?
decisions.ruling: Yes, except the old `# Generated by macos-setup: ...` line of each fragment, which goes: tools.toml is not shipped, so it carries no header. Each other comment line and each trailing comment of an old fragment line stays as a TOML comment on the same entry in tools.toml.

decisions.decision: In which order does a pack of macos/packs.toml list its members, and in which order are the packs?
decisions.ruling: In the order of MS/tools/packs.toml: the packs in the old file order, and the members of each pack in the order of its old tools list. This plan inserts each member at its old position.

decisions.decision: Which members get default = true when the old pack has no default list?
decisions.ruling: Every member. The old rule was "absent: every tool of the pack is a default", so iwork, ms-office, chat and cli-extras get default = true on each member.

decisions.decision: How does the sample values file select the 52 tools?
decisions.ruling: One empty [tools.<name>] table for each of the 52 tools, so the file selects every tool outside pack base, as MS/tests/setup-sync/sample-config/macos-setup.toml does. test:macos-tools then renders every Mac tool.
decisions.rejected: [packs.<name>] tables; they select only the default = true members.

decisions.decision: Does the plan add test cases?
decisions.ruling: No new test case. test:macos-tools renders every selected tool and parses every JSON, YAML and TOML output, so the selection of D7 is the test of the 52 tools.
decisions.rejected: One test case for each new tool.

decisions.decision: Which names does the check of the sample selection compare?
decisions.ruling: Only the tool names outside pack base. macos/examples/macos.toml also holds [tools.<name>] tables of base tools for their answers (P10 to P12); the check ignores them.
decisions.rejected: Compare every [tools.*] name with the old sample list.

decisions.decision: Does a security finding in content that this plan imports unchanged from macos-setup stop the run?
decisions.ruling: User ruling 2026-11-05, given at D14 of 2026-11-04-macos-tools-base-core for plans 11 to 14: no. A security finding in content that is byte for byte from macos-setup, apart from the changes that this plan names, is accepted for this import. It does not stop the run, and the content does not change. The run records each such finding as an open gap with its severity and location, for one security plan after the run. A finding in code that this plan writes or changes stops the run as before.
decisions.rejected: Stop on each finding in imported content.

gaps.text: macos/packs.toml:5 U3 removed the header sentence 'The import plans add the other members.', which 03-packs.md does not name · The wave review found the removal correct: this wave makes the sentence false, and no ruling protects it. Kept; settled with no ruling owed.

Security, medium, macos/tools/vorssaint/tools.toml:105-109 (U2): shared defaults hold a keep-awake assertion from launch with no time limit (keepAwakeAutoStart, defaultDurationMinutes=0, keepAwakeAllowDisplaySleep=false, launchAtLoginWanted at line 14) and clamshellPreferred applies closed-lid mode, so display-off and lid-close can stop acting as lock triggers on an unattended Mac; inferred from the app source, not tested on a Mac · Accepted under D10: imported byte for byte apart from the table prefix of D3; content unchanged, for the security plan after the run.

Security, medium, macos/tools/opencode/tools.toml:9 (U2): alias oc = "opencode --auto" auto-approves permissions not explicitly denied, so prompt injection from repo files or fetched content needs no approval step and can run commands as the user · Accepted under D10: imported byte for byte apart from the table prefix of D3; content unchanged, for the security plan after the run.

Security, medium, macos/tools/sill/tools.toml:6 (U2): third-party tap saffsanity/sill on a personal account (created 2026-10-14, 1 star); the owner controls the cask, URL and sha256 together, so a malicious owner or compromised account gets code execution at install or upgrade; opt-in tool · Accepted under D10: imported byte for byte apart from the table prefix of D3; content unchanged, for the security plan after the run.

Security, medium, macos/tools/orca/tools.toml:6 (U2): third-party tap stablyai/orca on the vendor's organization account (created 2026-05-01, 2 stars), with a cask that auto-updates outside brew and puts a CLI on PATH; a compromised or malicious vendor gets code execution as the user; opt-in tool · Accepted under D10: imported byte for byte apart from the table prefix of D3; content unchanged, for the security plan after the run.
